chapter: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
title: Armstrong returns from Europe and cuts Rex Stewart
summary: Prompted by Rex Stewart's account, Butler says Armstrong, written off while in Europe in 1934, came back with crystallised playing and killed the trumpet section on the first note.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Rex Stewart said something about a cutting session of some sort with Armstrong and they thought that Stewart played something -- it may have been 'West End Blues.' And he said everybody thought Stewart had got him and Armstrong came up there in a white suit --
The first or second note he snatched
was the F, right on the head.

Right on the head. You know when that was? When he come back from Europe. See, when he stayed in Europe, that was, I think, 1934, he stayed in Europe. And everybody said, "Louis is finished now because when you go to Europe, you're finished." It depends on the bman. He becomes more -- or his playing would become more crystallized. And each note he played would have meaning. It became more -- so when he come back (inaudible) and all the trumpets were down he said, "Yes, brothers." there looking and^The first thing (humming). He killed them. (Humming.)
